catalogue: Australian residential safe-movement, stair, ramp, barrier and handrail construction

objects.name: residential safe-movement and fall-protection system
objects.definition: The coordinated walking surfaces, stairs, ramps, landings, thresholds, handrails and fall-prevention barriers that allow people to move to and within a house or associated Class 10 building.
functions: Prevent falls from trafficable edges and openings

ncc_references.relationship: Coordinates the physical systems used for safe movement and fall prevention; performance thresholds remain constraints and analysis.

cad.pattern: Connected trafficable surfaces and protective edges
cad.placement: Along routes to and within the building
cad.opening: Coordinates doors, stair wells and trafficable-edge openings
cad.load: Walking, barrier and handrail actions transferred to supporting structure

notes: Fall height, rise, going, slope, headroom, opening limits and structural capacity are constraints or attributes, not extra solids.

objects.name: pedestrian circulation surface assembly
objects.definition: A floor, path, landing, tread or ramp surface and its supporting layers where a person walks while moving to or within a building.
functions: Receive the selected slip-resistant finish or treatment

cad.pattern: Continuous trafficable face following route geometry
cad.placement: On floors, steps, ramps and landings
cad.opening: Breaks only at controlled level changes and openings
cad.load: Pedestrian actions carried by substrate and structure

notes: Slip resistance belongs to the tested surface product and exposure condition, not to a generic invisible layer.

objects.name: residential stairway assembly
objects.definition: A complete construction of one or more flights and landings that provides stepped movement between floor levels, including supports, treads, risers or open-riser gaps, finishes, barriers and handrails where selected.
functions: Coordinate walking surfaces, edges, barriers and handholds

ncc_references.relationship: Contains physical flights, treads, risers and winders whose dimensions and consistency are checked against the selected path.

cad.pattern: Parametric sequence of steps between level datums
cad.placement: Within a stair well or along an external building-serving route
cad.opening: Occupies and defines a stair-well opening
cad.load: Pedestrian and self-weight actions transferred through stringers, walls, slabs or frames

notes: Housing Provisions do not give ordinary Class 1 and 10 stairs a universal minimum width; width remains a project and performance input.

objects.name: straight-flight stair assembly
objects.definition: A stairway whose flight or aligned flights rise in one plan direction without winders or a curved walking line.
functions: Use a constant straight nosing line

cad.pattern: Linear repeated tread array
cad.opening: Clear width and headroom zones remain analysis overlays
cad.load: Transferred along straight stringers or supporting construction

objects.name: quarter-turn stair assembly
objects.definition: A stairway that changes plan direction by about a quarter turn using a landing or permitted group of winders between flights.
functions: Fit a stair around a corner
Coordinate inside and outside strings or supports

cad.pattern: Two flights joined by quarter landing or winder group
cad.opening: Turn geometry preserves the measured walking line
cad.load: Carried by strings, landing frame and supports

notes: Landing and winder versions are alternative geometries and must not be merged into one undifferentiated turn solid.

objects.name: half-turn stair assembly
objects.definition: A stairway with adjacent flights running in opposing directions and connected by a half landing or permitted winder arrangement.
functions: Compact a larger rise into a shorter plan
Provide an intermediate rest or turning location

cad.pattern: Opposing parallel flights joined at turn
cad.opening: Central well and landing edges are explicit
cad.load: Transferred through stringers, landing frame and surrounding floor

notes: Dog-leg usually implies closely adjacent flights without a broad open well; it is not always a full synonym for every half-turn stair.

objects.name: winder stair assembly
objects.definition: A turning stairway using a controlled group of tapered treads instead of all or part of a quarter or half landing.
functions: Maintain a usable measured going along the required line
Fit turning geometry into a compact plan

cad.pattern: Radial or fan-shaped tread group within stair flight
cad.opening: Walking-line measurement is stored as a constraint path
cad.load: Each tapered tread bears on strings, newel or supporting frame

notes: Winder count and measurement rules are constraints; the drawable objects are the individual tapered treads and their supports.

objects.name: spiral stair assembly
objects.definition: A stairway whose tapered treads wind around a central pole or support while rising through a circular or near-circular plan.
functions: Support tapered treads from a centre and outer system
Carry a helical handrail and barrier

cad.pattern: Helical array of tapered treads
cad.opening: Central support and outside clear width remain distinct
cad.load: Transferred to centre pole, outer supports and landings

notes: Helical or curved stairs can lack a centre pole; they need a different support model even if casual speech calls them spiral.

objects.name: curved or geometric stair assembly
objects.definition: A stairway following a curved, elliptical or other non-rectilinear plan using purpose-set strings, treads, newels and handrails rather than a simple central-pole spiral arrangement.
functions: Follow a designed curved walking path
Carry curved strings, barriers and handrails

cad.pattern: Non-linear parametric tread and string sequence
cad.opening: Curved clear width and headroom are evaluated along the walking path
cad.load: Transferred through engineered curved strings, slabs or frames

notes: Every tread can differ; do not generate a curved stair by non-uniformly scaling one straight tread component.

objects.name: open-riser stair assembly
objects.definition: A stairway in which one or more vertical spaces between adjacent treads remain open rather than being closed by solid riser boards or faces.
functions: Leave open vertical space between treads
Coordinate opening limits with tread thickness and overlap

cad.pattern: Tread array with explicit vertical openings
cad.opening: Each clear riser gap is modelled and checked
cad.load: Treads supported independently by strings or brackets

notes: Open riser describes the missing closure; it does not mean the tread is structurally cantilevered or floating.

objects.name: closed-riser stair assembly
objects.definition: A stairway whose vertical spaces between successive treads are closed by riser boards, concrete faces, metal pans or another continuous construction.
functions: Support finishes or contribute to traditional timber tread stiffness where designed

cad.pattern: Alternating tread and solid riser faces
cad.opening: No uncontrolled opening between successive treads
cad.load: Carried by strings, slab or stair frame

objects.name: external building-serving stair assembly
objects.definition: A stairway outside the weather envelope that directly serves access to, from or within the building and is detailed for weather, drainage, durability and wet surface conditions.
functions: Resist weather exposure and transfer loads to external supports
not_synonyms: landscaping stair not serving a building

cad.pattern: Weather-exposed flights and landings
cad.placement: Outside building envelope on a delineated access route
cad.opening: Joints and perforations drain without creating unsafe gaps
cad.load: Transferred to external foundations, deck or building frame

notes: The ABCB distinguishes stairs serving the building from unrelated landscaping steps; scope must be resolved before applying Housing Provisions geometry.

objects.name: stair flight assembly
objects.definition: A continuous sloping run of steps between landings or floor levels, formed by its supports, treads, risers or openings, nosings, finishes and associated edge protection.
functions: Connect its lower and upper landings

cad.pattern: Repeated step modules along sloping datum
cad.opening: Open-riser gaps and side fall edges remain explicit
cad.load: Transferred through flight supports at bearings and anchors

notes: The flight is an assembly; rise and going are measurements of its geometry rather than separate building objects.

objects.name: residential building-serving ramp assembly
objects.definition: A sloping pedestrian construction serving an external doorway or located within a building, including its trafficable surface, supports, landings, joints, edge protection and handrails where selected.
functions: Provide pedestrian movement along a gradient
Carry a slip-resistant surface and associated protective components
not_synonyms: accessible ramp without selected accessibility path

ncc_references.relationship: Contains the physical ramp and landing surfaces checked for gradient, intervals and slip classification.

cad.pattern: Sloping planar run between level landings
cad.placement: At an external doorway or within the building
cad.opening: Door swings and thresholds are coordinated at landings
cad.load: Transferred through slab, beams, posts or ground support

notes: Housing ramp geometry is not automatically an AS 1428.1 accessible ramp; the selected regulatory path must be explicit.

objects.name: stair or ramp landing assembly
objects.definition: A substantially level trafficable platform at the top, bottom or intermediate point of a stairway or ramp, including its structure, substrate, finish, edges and connections.
functions: Connect flights, ramps, floors and doorways

cad.pattern: Level platform adjoining flights, ramps or doors
cad.placement: At route transitions and prescribed intervals
cad.opening: Door swings, stair wells and barrier lines are explicit
cad.load: Transferred to floor frame, slab, beams or posts

notes: Landing length and gradient are attributes checked against the applicable path; the physical landing contains multiple structural and finish objects.

objects.name: doorway threshold step assembly
objects.definition: A controlled stepped transition at a doorway where the threshold is above the adjoining surface, including the door sill, step treads and risers, landing interface and weathering details.
functions: Provide safe intermediate step geometry where required
Coordinate weatherproofing with the walking surface

cad.pattern: One or more step modules aligned to doorway
cad.placement: At external or internal door threshold
cad.opening: Extends across doorway width and clears door operation
cad.load: Supported by slab, landing or local frame

notes: Threshold, sill and step are related but different physical objects; the assembly keeps all three when present.

objects.name: fall-prevention barrier system
objects.definition: A continuous physical construction along a hazardous trafficable edge or relevant opening that resists people falling over, through or between its components.
functions: Transfer impact and pressure actions to supporting structure

ncc_references.relationship: Physical barrier components occupy the edge selected by fall-height and trafficable-surface constraints.

cad.pattern: Continuous protected-edge run segmented at corners and transitions
cad.placement: Along trafficable edges, stairs, ramps, landings, decks and relevant openings
cad.opening: Gates and junctions preserve barrier continuity
cad.load: Transferred through posts, panels, rails and anchors to host structure

notes: Required height, allowed openings and non-climbability are measurements of the assembled geometry, not separate barrier products.

objects.name: stair or ramp handrail system
objects.definition: A continuous graspable rail and its brackets, posts, joiners, returns, end fittings and anchors provided beside a stair flight or ramp to assist balance and movement.
functions: Transfer user actions into a wall, barrier or posts

ncc_references.relationship: Contains the physical rail and support fittings whose height, extent and continuity are checked.

cad.pattern: Continuous rail path parallel to stair nosings or ramp surface
cad.placement: Along selected side of stair flight or ramp
cad.opening: Returns and joints do not create a broken handhold
cad.load: Transferred through brackets or posts to structure

notes: A barrier top rail can also serve as the handrail only when its physical profile, height and continuity satisfy both roles.

objects.name: alpine external trafficable access assembly
objects.definition: An external stairway, ramp, access bridge or similar trafficable structure serving a building in an alpine area and detailed for snow, ice, drainage, open surfaces and open barrier construction under the selected path.
functions: Provide external access in alpine conditions
Reduce accumulation on the egress surface
Coordinate open barriers with snow-shedding hazards

cad.pattern: Weather-exposed open stair, ramp or bridge assembly
cad.opening: Mesh apertures and barrier openness are modelled as product geometry
cad.load: Pedestrian, snow and environmental actions carried to supports

notes: Alpine provisions modify the external assembly; they are not represented by a snow tag attached to an ordinary closed walking surface.

objects.name: stair stringer support system
objects.definition: The one or more sloping structural members and associated cleats, housings, brackets, bearings and anchors that support a stair flight's treads and risers.
functions: Transfer flight loads to landings or floors
Control flight line and step set-out

cad.pattern: One or more sloping support members beside or below treads
cad.opening: Cut-outs, housings and bracket holes follow tread set-out
cad.load: Bending, shear, bearing and connection actions

notes: Stringer, string and carriage overlap in trade speech; the stored object must preserve actual section and support geometry.

objects.name: cut timber stair stringer
objects.definition: A sloping timber member with a stepped upper profile cut to form horizontal tread seats and vertical riser faces for direct support of the steps.
functions: Transfer step loads along the flight

cad.pattern: Sloping member with repeated stepped cuts
cad.placement: Below tread ends or intermediate tread line
cad.opening: Cuts retain documented throat depth
cad.load: Tread reactions delivered through notched section

notes: Open stringer describes visible tread support geometry and must not be confused with an open-riser gap.

objects.name: housed timber stair stringer
objects.definition: A sloping timber string with grooves or housings cut into its inside face to receive tread and riser ends, usually tightened with wedges in traditional construction.
functions: Provide a clean outside string face

cad.pattern: Sloping solid member with repeated internal grooves
cad.placement: At side of timber stair flight
cad.opening: Housings match individual tread and riser ends
cad.load: Step reactions transferred through housed joints

objects.name: steel plate stair stringer
objects.definition: A flat or profiled steel plate running along or beneath a stair flight and carrying welded or bolted tread brackets, cleats or pans.
functions: Provide a slender fabricated flight edge or spine
Transfer loads through welded or bolted connections

cad.pattern: Sloping plate with repetitive tread connections
cad.opening: Bolt holes and bracket welds are explicit at fabrication detail
cad.load: Bending, shear, torsion and connection actions

notes: Proprietary steel-string details vary; preserve the selected plate profile, tread connections, end plates and corrosion-protection system as product-specific geometry.

objects.name: steel channel or hollow-section stair stringer
objects.definition: A channel, rectangular hollow section or other rolled or formed steel section used as a sloping stair-flight support with attached tread brackets or pans.
functions: Receive fabricated tread connections and end plates

cad.pattern: Sloping structural section with bracket stations
cad.placement: At stair sides or below treads
cad.opening: Section ends, drainage and access holes remain fabricated details
cad.load: Structural flight actions transferred through section and connections

objects.name: central mono-stringer stair support
objects.definition: A stair support arrangement using one central sloping beam or fabricated spine with individual brackets or arms extending to carry each tread.
functions: Support the flight from a central spine
Create open sides beneath tread ends

cad.pattern: One central sloping beam with repeated lateral arms
cad.opening: Clearances around spine and tread brackets remain visible
cad.load: Combined bending and torsion transferred at supports

notes: Floating describes appearance, not a structural system; a central spine, wall cantilever or hidden twin strings need different objects.

objects.name: stair tread
objects.definition: The substantially horizontal trafficable part of one step on which a person places a foot, including its front nosing geometry but excluding any separately applied finish or nosing strip.
functions: Provide the walking surface of a step

cad.pattern: Repeated horizontal step element
cad.placement: Across stair flight between or over supports
cad.opening: Rear gap and open-riser clearance remain explicit
cad.load: Pedestrian point and distributed actions carried to supports

notes: Going is measured geometry between nosings; it is not the same as physical tread depth and is not another board.

objects.name: timber stair tread
objects.definition: A solid, laminated or engineered timber tread shaped with a nosing and fixed to strings, housings, cleats or brackets.
functions: Receive riser joints, nosing inserts and finish

cad.pattern: Rectangular or tapered timber panel with profiled front edge
cad.placement: On timber or steel stair supports
cad.opening: Housings and fixing holes match selected string system
cad.load: Spans between supports with local footfall actions

objects.name: precast concrete stair tread or step unit
objects.definition: A factory-formed concrete step unit with an integral tread and often riser face, bearing seats and cast-in or drilled connections to a supporting stair frame.
functions: Receive a slip-resistant finish or formed surface

cad.pattern: Repeated precast step units on frame or supports
cad.placement: Across concrete or steel stair support
cad.opening: Unit joints and bearing gaps remain explicit
cad.load: Self weight and pedestrian actions through bearings and connectors

objects.name: steel plate stair tread
objects.definition: A fabricated flat, folded or chequered steel plate forming one stair tread and attached to brackets, stringers or a stair pan system.
functions: Receive folded nosing and anti-slip treatment

cad.pattern: Folded or flat step panel
cad.placement: Between steel stringers or on brackets
cad.opening: Drainage or fixing holes are product-specific
cad.load: Plate bending transferred to side or central brackets

notes: A raised plate pattern does not by itself establish the required tested slip classification.

objects.name: metal grating stair tread
objects.definition: An open metal grating panel made with bearing bars and cross bars, commonly fitted with a front nosing and side plates for bolting to stair supports.
functions: Pass water, snow and small debris
Transfer footfall loads through bearing bars

cad.pattern: Open bar grid with solid side plates and front nosing
cad.placement: Across external or alpine stair supports
cad.opening: Apertures are physical geometry and checked for the selected use
cad.load: Bearing bars span to side plates or supports

notes: Expanded mesh and welded or pressure-locked grating have different geometry; preserve the selected product family.

objects.name: metal stair pan
objects.definition: A folded steel tray forming the underside, rear and front containment for a tread infill such as concrete, screed, stone or another finish.
functions: Form the riser and nosing edge where designed

cad.pattern: Repeated folded tray
cad.opening: Receives documented infill and edge treatment
cad.load: Pan and infill act through their designed connection

notes: The pan and its concrete or finish infill are separate physical objects with different quantities and evidence.

objects.name: stair pan tread infill
objects.definition: The concrete, screed, resin, stone or other solid fill placed inside a metal stair pan to create the final tread body and receive the walking finish.
functions: Provide tread mass and surface support
Receive the final finish or slip treatment

cad.pattern: Solid fill following inside of stair pan
cad.opening: Stops at nosing inserts and joints
cad.load: Supported and contained by pan

objects.name: stair tread finish layer
objects.definition: The exposed walking finish applied over a structural stair tread, such as timber overlay, tile, stone, resilient flooring, carpet or coating.
functions: Carry the evidenced slip classification where tested as the finished product

cad.pattern: Thin finish following tread and optional riser
cad.opening: Joints and inserts interrupt finish explicitly
cad.load: Pedestrian wear transferred to substrate

notes: A material name alone does not prove a slip class; retain the tested product, surface condition and report.

objects.name: stair tread nosing
objects.definition: The front edge or projecting profile of a stair tread that defines the visible step edge and the datum from which stair going and barrier or handrail heights may be measured.
functions: Define the front edge of the tread
Protect or shape the tread edge
Receive an applied slip-resistant strip or insert where selected

cad.pattern: Continuous front-edge profile across each tread
cad.opening: Stops or mitres at strings and edge trims
cad.load: Local footfall and impact at tread edge

notes: Nosing is tread geometry; a separately applied slip-resistant nosing strip is another object.

objects.name: slip-resistant stair nosing strip assembly
objects.definition: A tested strip, carrier profile or bonded insert fixed at or near the tread nosing to provide a defined slip-resistant walking band.
functions: Improve grip at the tread edge
Mark and protect the nosing where the selected product also provides contrast

cad.pattern: Narrow strip across full usable tread width
cad.opening: Fixing holes or adhesive bed follow selected product
cad.load: Direct foot traffic and edge impact

notes: Non-slip is not an absolute property; store the test method, classification, exposure and product evidence.

objects.name: stair nosing carrier profile
objects.definition: A metal or rigid polymer extrusion fixed to the tread edge that supports a replaceable slip-resistant insert and protects the nosing.
functions: Provide a fixing interface to the substrate

cad.pattern: Extruded profile following nosing
cad.opening: Insert recess and fastener holes are explicit
cad.load: Footfall and impact transferred through fixings

objects.name: stair nosing slip-resistant insert
objects.definition: A replaceable abrasive, elastomeric or composite strip locked or bonded into a stair nosing carrier to form the exposed slip-resistant band.
functions: Allow worn surface replacement where the system permits

cad.pattern: Narrow exposed band within carrier
cad.opening: Insert joints align with product lengths
cad.load: Direct foot traffic

objects.name: full-tread slip-resistant safety plate
objects.definition: A rigid textured plate fixed over most or all of a stair tread surface to provide a durable slip-resistant overlay and often an integral nosing.
functions: Cover the tread with a gripping surface
Protect a worn or exposed substrate
Provide an integral front edge where designed

cad.pattern: Textured overlay matching tread plan
cad.opening: Fixing holes and joints follow product
cad.load: Foot traffic transferred to tread substrate

objects.name: stair riser closure
objects.definition: The vertical or near-vertical physical face closing the space between successive stair treads, formed by a board, panel, concrete face, folded pan or other solid construction.
functions: Close the vertical space between treads
Connect or brace adjacent tread construction where designed

cad.pattern: Repeated vertical panel between adjacent treads
cad.opening: Joints to treads and strings are explicit
cad.load: Closure load and any designed tread bracing transferred at joints

notes: Riser can mean a physical closure or a vertical dimension; this object is only the physical closure.

objects.name: timber stair riser board
objects.definition: A solid or engineered timber board housed or fixed between stair treads and strings to form the closed vertical face of a traditional timber step.
functions: Engage with tread grooves or fixings
Receive paint, clear finish or applied lining

cad.pattern: Rectangular board repeated between treads
cad.placement: In housed strings or behind tread edges
cad.opening: Ends fit string housings
cad.load: Supported by tread and string joints

objects.name: open-riser clear opening
objects.definition: The actual clear void between the rear of one tread and the underside or front edge of the tread above in an open-riser stair.
functions: Leave the stair visually and physically open
Provide geometry for the passage-limit check

cad.pattern: Repeated void bounded by adjacent treads
cad.opening: The object is the measured clear opening
cad.load: No load; bounded by structural treads

notes: The 125 mm sphere is a checking tool or constraint, not a ball-shaped building object.

objects.name: winder stair tread
objects.definition: A tapered stair tread used within a turning flight, with different inner and outer depths and a going measured on the applicable walking line.
functions: Provide one step through a stair turn
Connect inner and outer stair supports

cad.pattern: Fan-shaped or polygonal tread
cad.placement: Within winder group at stair turn
cad.opening: Clear walking line stored separately from solid tread
cad.load: Spans between strings, newel and brackets

objects.name: spiral stair tread
objects.definition: A radial tapered tread with a centre-pole connection and an outer edge supporting or connecting to the spiral stair barrier and handrail system.
functions: Carry its outer edge and barrier connection

cad.pattern: Repeated radial wedge around centre pole
cad.placement: At one elevation increment on spiral stair
cad.opening: Clear width begins outside centre obstruction
cad.load: Cantilever or bracket reaction into centre and outer system

objects.name: stair soffit lining
objects.definition: A board or sheet lining fixed beneath a stair flight to create a finished sloping underside and conceal strings, tread backs or services.
functions: Provide a substrate for decorative or required protective finishes

cad.pattern: Sloping lining plane below flight
cad.opening: Access and service openings remain separate
cad.load: Non-structural lining supported by battens or frame

objects.name: stair skirt board
objects.definition: A sloping finish board fitted at the junction of a stair flight and wall, following the tread and riser profile or covering the wall-side string.
functions: Provide a durable edge for wall finish

cad.pattern: Sloping trim following step profile
cad.opening: Fits around tread and riser ends
cad.load: Finish board fixed to wall or string

notes: A skirt can conceal a wall string but should not be assigned its structural role unless it actually carries treads.

objects.name: stair tread support bracket
objects.definition: A steel, aluminium or timber bracket projecting from a stringer, spine, wall or post to support and fix one stair tread.
functions: Connect the tread to its main support
Transfer vertical and torsional tread actions

cad.pattern: Repeated bracket at each tread station
cad.placement: On stringer, spine or wall support
cad.opening: Bolt and screw holes align to fabrication
cad.load: Tread reactions into main support

objects.name: stair stringer connection cleat
objects.definition: An angle, plate, block or fabricated fitting connecting a stair stringer end or side to a landing beam, floor frame, wall or support post.
functions: Connect the stringer to supporting structure
Transfer shear, tension and lateral actions

cad.pattern: Discrete fitting at stringer support
cad.placement: At top, bottom or intermediate string connection
cad.opening: Fastener pattern is explicit
cad.load: Stringer reactions into host

objects.name: housed-stair tread or riser wedge
objects.definition: A tapered timber piece driven and glued into the wedge-shaped pocket behind a housed tread or riser end to tighten it against the string housing.
functions: Hold tread or riser against bearing face
Reduce movement and squeaking when correctly fitted

cad.pattern: Small tapered block at each housed joint
cad.placement: Behind tread or riser within string
cad.opening: Fits documented wedge pocket
cad.load: Joint compression and retention

objects.name: stair tread-to-riser glue block
objects.definition: A small timber block glued and sometimes pinned or screwed beneath the junction of a tread and riser to reinforce the corner and limit relative movement.

cad.pattern: Short repeated block behind tread-riser corner
cad.opening: Stops clear of strings and services
cad.load: Local joint restraint

objects.name: stair assembly screw, bolt or fixing
objects.definition: A selected screw, bolt, coach screw, anchor, pin or proprietary fastener securing stair treads, risers, brackets, stringers or landing components.

cad.pattern: Discrete fasteners at documented connection pattern
cad.placement: At tread, riser, bracket, string or landing joints
cad.opening: Predrilled hole or anchor socket where required
cad.load: Shear, tension and clamp force

notes: Fastener selection is connection-specific; one generic stair screw must not be copied into steel, concrete and timber hosts.

objects.name: stair stringer top connection assembly
objects.definition: The bearing, notch, hanger, cleat, end plate, bolts and local floor framing that connect the top of a stair stringer to an upper landing or floor edge.
functions: Coordinate the top tread and landing level

cad.pattern: Detailed support node at upper string end
cad.placement: At upper landing or floor trimmer
cad.opening: Coordinates stair-well edge and finish
cad.load: Upper flight reaction into floor or landing

objects.name: stair stringer bottom connection assembly
objects.definition: The seat cut, bearing plate, cleat, anchor and local substrate that support and restrain the lower end of a stair stringer at a floor, footing or landing.
functions: Coordinate the first riser with finished floor level

cad.pattern: Detailed support node at lower string end
cad.placement: On lower floor, slab, landing or footing
cad.opening: Anchor and damp separation follow host
cad.load: Lower flight reaction into support

objects.name: stair stringer bearing seat
objects.definition: A shaped timber seat, steel plate, masonry ledge or concrete pad providing direct bearing beneath a stair stringer end.
functions: Separate the string from an unsuitable or wet substrate where detailed

cad.pattern: Local bearing pad beneath string end
cad.placement: At top or bottom stair support
cad.opening: Anchor holes remain separate
cad.load: Compression and local bearing

objects.name: stair or ramp landing deck substrate
objects.definition: The structural or load-spreading panel, boards or slab surface forming the body of a landing beneath its exposed walking finish.
functions: Carry pedestrian loads to landing supports
Receive the final finish and edge components

cad.pattern: Level deck or slab field
cad.opening: Stair well and service openings are trimmed
cad.load: Pedestrian loads to joists, beams, walls or slab

objects.name: landing walking-surface finish
objects.definition: The exposed finish on a stair or ramp landing, including the slip-resistant treatment near a stair edge where that treatment is provided by the surface rather than a separate strip.
functions: Carry slip-resistance evidence for the selected exposure

cad.pattern: Finish field following landing plan
cad.opening: Stops at nosing strip, threshold and joints
cad.load: Foot traffic and wear

objects.name: stair or ramp landing support frame
objects.definition: The beams, joists, trimmers, posts, ledgers and connections supporting a framed landing between stair flights, ramp runs or a doorway.
functions: Carry flight or ramp reactions where connected
Transfer loads to walls, posts or foundations

cad.pattern: Rectangular or shaped framing grid
cad.opening: Stair well edges use explicit trimmers
cad.load: Landing, barrier and connected flight reactions

objects.name: landing support beam
objects.definition: A horizontal timber or steel member carrying landing joists, deck edges or stair-stringer reactions between posts, walls or other supports.

cad.pattern: Horizontal primary member at landing edge
cad.opening: Connections and notches are explicit
cad.load: Bending, shear and local connection reactions

objects.name: landing support post
objects.definition: A vertical timber, steel or concrete member supporting an elevated stair or ramp landing and transferring its loads to a footing or lower structure.
functions: Provide a connection point for bracing where required

cad.pattern: Vertical support below landing corner or beam
cad.opening: Bracing and connections remain explicit
cad.load: Compression, bending and lateral actions

objects.name: landing edge apron or fascia
objects.definition: A vertical board, plate or trim closing and finishing the exposed edge of a landing frame below the trafficable surface.
functions: Provide an interface for side-mounted barrier brackets where designed

cad.pattern: Vertical perimeter strip
cad.opening: Side-mount brackets and drainage gaps are explicit
cad.load: Finish load unless specifically structural

objects.name: ramp trafficable deck or slab
objects.definition: The continuous sloping structural surface of a ramp, formed by a concrete slab, timber or composite decking, sheet panel, steel plate or grating.
functions: Define the physical gradient and crossfall
Receive the final slip-resistant finish or surface treatment

cad.pattern: Continuous sloping surface between landings
cad.opening: Joints, drains and penetrations remain explicit
cad.load: Pedestrian loads into ramp structure or ground

objects.name: framed ramp support assembly
objects.definition: The sloping beams or stringers, joists, bearers, posts, bracing and connections supporting an elevated timber, steel or composite ramp deck.
functions: Transfer loads to posts, walls or footings
Provide lateral stability and landing connections

cad.pattern: Sloping framing grid between landing supports
cad.opening: Bracing and services preserve clear route
cad.load: Ramp, barrier and handrail actions to foundations

objects.name: ramp stringer or sloping support beam
objects.definition: A primary sloping timber or steel member carrying an elevated ramp deck between landings or support frames.

cad.pattern: Parallel sloping members
cad.opening: Connection holes and notches remain explicit
cad.load: Bending and shear from deck

objects.name: ramp slip-resistant finish
objects.definition: The tested exposed ramp surface or applied coating, sheet, strip or aggregate treatment providing the required slip-resistance classification for its expected wet or dry condition.
functions: Carry the product's tested surface classification

cad.pattern: Continuous finish following ramp plane
cad.opening: Expansion joints and drains interrupt finish
cad.load: Foot traffic and weather exposure

objects.name: ramp movement-joint cover
objects.definition: A trafficable cover plate or proprietary profile bridging a movement or construction joint across a ramp or landing while allowing the intended relative movement.

cad.pattern: Linear profile crossing full ramp width

objects.name: openable-window supplementary barrier assembly

objects.name: barrier end post
